subject: Post-demo: Model finalists, cost/latency constraints & next-step asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@synapsehealth.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@syntheticsynapse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Model finalists, cost/latency constraints & next-step asks

Hi Mike / Elena —

Thanks again for the demo slot earlier. Quick recap from our side and a recommended shortlist for the PoC based on the use case you described (automated triage + clinician summarization for outpatient referral notes):

- Customer constraints we captured:
  * 99th-percentile latency target <= 450ms token-response for real-time drafts
  * Batch summarize nightly for older backlog (throughput-oriented)
  * Hard cap on inference spend: target unit cost <= $0.0009 per token once batched
  * PHI must never leave Synapse VPC for private deployment phase (later stage)

- Shortlist & rationale (initial):
  1) LlamaX-Alpha (quantized 8-bit) — best latency/cost balance for short context, strong instruction-following, lowest per-token cost in hosted tests.
  2) MedDialog-7B (fp16) — higher quality on clinical prompts in our evals; slightly higher latency and cost, but fewer hallucinations on entities.
  3) RedCore-13B-int4 — highest quality for long-context summarization; higher memory and cost, but valuable for the nightly backlog pipeline.

I've attached the benchmark summary and the prompt set we used (prompt_set_clinical_nonepi_v1.txt). Please review the numbers and flag any weights we should prioritize (latency vs quality).

Next steps we recommend:
- You: confirm priority (latency vs recall vs hallucination risk) and procurement contacts for pilot.
- Us: run a focused throughput/latency sweep on your three most-likely input shapes (we'll need a 1000-record sample).
- Schedule a 30-min check-in: propose Tue 09/14 10:00am PT.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:07:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Proposed eval plan + quick checks for Synapse (notes for Tue)

Team —

I pulled the attached benchmarks into a short eval plan. Key technical notes to discuss on Tue:

- Test shapes: 1) short clinician prompt (<=128 tokens), 2) medium note (512 tokens), 3) long summarization (2k tokens). We'll run latency at 99th/95th and per-token unit cost.
- LlamaX-Alpha: best 95th latency in our 8-bit path (~220ms for shape #1) and lowest cost. Known weakness: entity hallucination edge cases — mitigate with a light verification pass (regexp + medical NER).
- MedDialog-7B: stronger precision on clinical entities; expect ~1.3x cost and 1.4x latency vs LlamaX-Alpha for short prompts.
- RedCore-13B-int4: excellent long-context coherence; will need dedicated nodes for nightly batch; throughput is efficient once warmed (KV caching).

Attachments I pushed to drive: the prompt set you used, a quick regression alert playbook, and the benchmark CSV Aditya already shared. For the pilot, suggest we:
  A) Run side-by-side on a 1k de-id sample (Mike to provide).
  B) Measure three KPIs: clinician acceptance rate (binary), hallucination rate on entity checks, 99th percentile latency.
  C) For hosted pilot keep model variants in routing with automated fallback (MedDialog -> LlamaX if unavailable). For private phase we can pin models.

I'll prepare a short eval script and lightweight scoring harness so results are reproducible.

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Mike / Elena —

Great — thanks for confirming priorities and procurement lead. Quick action items ahead of our Tue sync: 

1) Synapse: please drop the 1k de-id sample in the Drive link (share with redwood-evals@redwood.com) and confirm the expected peak concurrent clinician flows (estimate).
2) Redwood (Karthik + Marissa): run the three-shape sweep and upload the result CSV to the drive by Tue 09/14 08:30 PT so we can review live.
3) Procurement: Elena, could you share the person who will own the MSA and SOC2 checklist? If you prefer we can open the enterprise intake ticket and pre-fill fields to save your team time.

Proposed pilot plan summary (for procurement):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week prep, 3-week pilot runs, 1-week wrap + SME review)
- Models in scope: LlamaX-Alpha (primary short-latency path), MedDialog-7B (high-precision short path), RedCore-13B-int4 (nightly long-context batch)
- Success criteria: 90% clinician acceptance on draft suggestions OR 30% time-saved on triage tasks with <=1% critical hallucination rate
- Cost guardrail: automated alerting at 20% over expected spend to pause routing and notify both teams

If that summary looks good I'll convert into a PoC one-pager and a short SOW draft for procurement. Meeting invite sent for Tue 09/14 10am PT.

Cheers,
Aditya
